$source_primary: Fowler, Refactoring: Improving the Design of Existing Code (2nd ed., 2018), Chapter 3 'Bad Smells in Code'
$source_extension: Ousterhout, A Philosophy of Software Design (2nd ed., 2021), Chapters 5-7
$grouping_source: Informal grouping popularized by Kerievsky's Refactoring to Patterns (2004) — Fowler's own presentation is alphabetical
$note: Skills reference this list via {{CODE_SMELLS_CHECKLIST}}. Keep entries concise — one-sentence diagnostic, one-sentence fix direction.

categories.name: Bloaters
categories.description: Code/classes/methods that have grown so large they're hard to work with. Usually accrete over time, rarely born this way.

smells.name: Long Function
smells.diagnostic: A method longer than a screenful — or whose body needs comments to navigate.
smells.fix: Extract Function along the comments/paragraphs. If the method mostly dispatches, consider Replace Conditional with Polymorphism.

smells.name: Long Parameter List
smells.diagnostic: More than 3-4 params, or a mix of params the caller has to compute together each time.
smells.fix: Introduce Parameter Object. If some params come from another object, Preserve Whole Object.

smells.name: Large Class
smells.diagnostic: A class with many fields/methods that seems to do too much. Probably has multiple responsibilities.
smells.fix: Extract Class along cohesion boundaries — which fields move together with which methods?

smells.name: Primitive Obsession
smells.diagnostic: Strings, ints, booleans used where a small domain type would encode the invariants (phone numbers, money, coordinates).
smells.fix: Replace Data Value with Object. Even a tiny wrapper pays for itself on validation.

smells.name: Data Clumps
smells.diagnostic: The same 3+ fields appear together in many classes, method signatures, or parameter lists.
smells.fix: Extract Class for the clump. If they travel with behavior, the class will attract methods too.

categories.name: Object-Orientation Abusers
categories.description: Cases where OO mechanisms are present but misapplied.

smells.name: Repeated Switches
smells.diagnostic: The same switch/if-else ladder on a type code appears in 3+ places.
smells.fix: Replace Conditional with Polymorphism. Pushes the branches into subclasses or a strategy object.

smells.name: Refused Bequest
smells.diagnostic: A subclass inherits fields/methods it doesn't want or that don't apply.
smells.fix: Replace Inheritance with Delegation, or extract a common interface and have both implement it.

smells.name: Alternative Classes with Different Interfaces
smells.diagnostic: Two classes do the same job but with different method names/signatures.
smells.fix: Rename to align interfaces, then extract a common supertype. Or keep one and delete the other.

categories.name: Change Preventers
categories.description: Smells that make changing the code expensive — one conceptual change requires many edits.

smells.name: Divergent Change
smells.diagnostic: ONE class changes for MANY unrelated reasons (billing rules AND reporting format AND email templates).
smells.fix: Split the class along the axes of change. Each resulting class changes for one reason.

smells.name: Shotgun Surgery
smells.diagnostic: ONE conceptual change (e.g. adding a currency) requires edits in MANY classes. Inverse of Divergent Change.
smells.fix: Move Method/Field to consolidate the responsibility. The next change should touch one class.

smells.name: Parallel Inheritance Hierarchies
smells.diagnostic: Every time you add a subclass to one hierarchy, you have to add one to another hierarchy.
smells.fix: Collapse the two hierarchies or use composition/delegation.

categories.name: Dispensables
categories.description: Code that exists but shouldn't — its removal makes the system cleaner.

smells.name: Comments
smells.diagnostic: A comment explaining WHAT code does (not why). Often the comment was written because the code wasn't readable.
smells.fix: Rewrite the code so the comment is redundant. Keep comments only for WHY — constraints, non-obvious context, decisions.

smells.name: Duplicated Code
smells.diagnostic: The same expression/block appears in 2+ places. Or the same algorithm in slightly different forms.
smells.fix: Extract Function / Pull Up Method. Don't apply DRY blindly — see Rule of Three (Hunt & Thomas).

smells.name: Lazy Element
smells.diagnostic: A class/function that doesn't do enough to justify its existence (one-liner delegating to another).
smells.fix: Inline Function / Collapse Hierarchy. Every element should earn its keep.

smells.name: Data Class
smells.diagnostic: A class with only fields and getters/setters, no behavior.
smells.fix: Move behavior that operates on these fields INTO the class. If it genuinely has no behavior, consider making it a value object / record.

smells.name: Dead Code
smells.diagnostic: Code that isn't called by anything live.
smells.fix: Delete it. Version control remembers. Dead code wastes attention on every read.

smells.name: Speculative Generality
smells.diagnostic: Abstract classes, hooks, or parameters added 'in case we need it later' but never used.
smells.fix: Remove the unused flexibility. Add it back when a real requirement arrives.

categories.name: Couplers
categories.description: Smells that indicate modules are too aware of each other's internals.

smells.name: Feature Envy
smells.diagnostic: A method uses another class's data more than its own — walks through get/set calls to do its work.
smells.fix: Move Method to the class whose data it uses. Or Extract the envious portion and move just that.

smells.name: Inappropriate Intimacy
smells.diagnostic: Two classes know too much about each other's private parts. Changes in one usually require changes in the other.
smells.fix: Move Method/Field to consolidate, Extract Class for the shared concept, or invert the dependency direction.

smells.name: Message Chains
smells.diagnostic: A caller navigates through a chain of gets: `a.getB().getC().getD().doThing()`. Callers are coupled to the entire navigation structure.
smells.fix: Hide Delegate on `a` so callers say `a.doThing()`. Law of Demeter.

smells.name: Middle Man
smells.diagnostic: A class that does nothing but delegate to another class. More than half its methods are pure delegation.
smells.fix: Remove Middle Man — talk to the delegate directly. Or Inline the middle man if it's a simple wrapper.

smells.name: Insider Trading
smells.diagnostic: Modules passing data/methods back and forth through back channels (friend classes, private internals, undocumented conventions).
smells.fix: Surface the coupling as an explicit interface, or break it with a Mediator. Hidden coupling is more expensive than visible coupling.

smells.name: Mysterious Name
smells.diagnostic: A variable/function/class name that doesn't say what it does. `processData`, `handleItem`, `doStuff`.
smells.fix: Rename with intent. If you can't name it clearly, the thing probably doesn't have a clear job — fix that first.

smells.name: Global Data
smells.diagnostic: Shared mutable state that anything can modify from anywhere.
smells.fix: Encapsulate behind an accessor; or eliminate by threading state explicitly. Global data is action at a distance.

smells.name: Mutable Data
smells.diagnostic: Fields/variables whose values change in non-obvious ways, especially across threads or callbacks.
smells.fix: Favor immutability. When mutation is necessary, restrict its scope (Encapsulate Variable, Split Phase).

smells.name: Loops
smells.diagnostic: Explicit loops where a pipeline (map/filter/reduce/forEach) would express intent more clearly.
smells.fix: Replace Loop with Pipeline — when the loop is 'transform each, then filter, then sum', pipelines read better.

smells.name: Temporary Field
smells.diagnostic: A field that's only set in some circumstances; null/undefined most of the time. Reader has to guess when it's valid.
smells.fix: Extract Class for the case where the field IS populated; or use Introduce Null Object for the empty case.

categories.name: Module-Depth Extensions (Ousterhout)
categories.description: Not in Fowler's list but equally diagnostic. See docs/DESIGN_TESTS.md §Module-depth.

smells.name: Pass-through Method
smells.diagnostic: A method that does little except call another method with a similar signature. `Controller.findUser(id) { return service.findUser(id) }`.
smells.fix: Delete the pass-through. Let the caller hit the service directly. Or, if the wrapper is adding a concern (auth, logging), name the concern and make the method about THAT.

smells.name: Pass-through Variable
smells.diagnostic: A variable threaded through N function/method signatures, used only at the bottom. Every layer in between is coupled to it.
smells.fix: Introduce a context object, thread-local, or dependency injection. Or lift the consumer up so the intermediate layers aren't involved.
